title: A runner started in a clone that is a linked worktree of another checkout blocks every item: its workers get worktrees in that checkout and the headless guard refuses their writes
goal: backlog.py selfcheck and autopilot.py runner start refuse a manager clone whose git-common-dir is not its own git-dir (a linked worktree of another checkout), naming the other checkout and saying to use a real clone, so a runner never starts where Claude Code puts its workers' isolation worktrees outside the runner's project; a planted test builds a repository with a linked worktree and sees the refusal; found by the first supervised run (ST-opjydjc3), Stage 1: exit 0, cause blocked, nothing landed

run: import subprocess,sys; g=lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git',*a],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip(); linked=g('rev-parse','--git-common-dir')!=g('rev-parse','--git-dir'); out=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','selfcheck'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout; sys.exit(0 if (not linked) or 'linked worktree' in out else 1)

notes: Stage 1 repeated in a real clone (own .git) still blocked: the guard refused the worker because its isolation worktree is a sibling of the runner's worktree. A linked-worktree manager clone is a real hazard (workers land in the other checkout) but not the only cause; the first cause to fix is BG-svzlkygp. Keep, lower the priority, or drop once BG-svzlkygp is fixed and Stage 1 lands in a linked clone: the manager decides.
